o1.biggest_strength: It answers the brief the way an operator wants it: a glance table with goal and measure per email, skip rules, real trigger logic off the recurring-task event, subject lines with character counts, and a drop table that puts a number on every cut.
o1.biggest_mistake: It deletes the Pro email outright and spends the fifth slot re-pitching recurring tasks, so the series has no path to paid conversion and the last email repeats email 2.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep a calm Pro email at day 14 for users who already made a recurring task or added a second device (replace the duplicate recurring nudge), and fix the one loose target: both habits is 8% by day 7, so measure it at day 7, not day 14.

o2.biggest_strength: Commercially the smarter shape: it keeps a gentle Pro email but moves it to day 14 for engaged users only, and the five emails cover more distinct ground (empty the head, repeats, second device, calm restart, Pro) with simpler sequencing.
o2.biggest_mistake: Loose production detail — no subject-line length checks, and 'sign in with this email' is the kind of small inaccuracy that ships; the second-device email also sits on a fixed day 3 rather than using the recurring-task trigger to time it.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add per-email skip rules and a at-a-glance table with goal and measure, verify subject lengths and fix the sign-in wording, and trigger the second-device email off the recurring-task event so the sequence builds habit on habit.

reason: Both got the data and the two-habit thesis right, but Output 1 gives me a table I can hand to the team, checks the numbers and subject lengths, and uses the triggers properly; I'd only push back on it killing the Pro email. Output 2 has the better revenue call but is looser to run.
